description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

latest_release.name: 7.22.0 Call-site variance
latest_release.body:
New AI, UX and `@template` syntax features.

## Features

- **Call-site variance**: `covariant` or `contravariant` before a type argument makes one param accept a generic of any subtype (or supertype) of it, without changing the class's template. As with `Box<*>`, values then go one way only: from a `Box<covariant Node>` you read `Node`, but can't put anything in. (#15096, @alies-dev)
  ```php
  /** @param Handler<covariant Node> $handler */
  function register(Handler $handler): void {}

  register(new LeafHandler()); // a Handler<LeafNode>: no issue (was InvalidArgument)
  ```
- **`psalm --explain=<issue>`** prints an issue's documentation (what it means, an example, how to fix it) from the installed version, offline and without a config. It takes the issue type, its shortcode or its psalm.dev link. (#15066, @alies-dev, @roxblnfk)
  ```bash
  vendor/bin/psalm --explain=PossiblyNullArgument
  vendor/bin/psalm --explain=078
  vendor/bin/psalm --explain=https://psalm.dev/078
  ```
- **AI coding agents**: when Psalm runs under an agent (`CLAUDECODE`, `CURSOR_AGENT`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `AI_AGENT`, …), it prints the `compact` format (one line per issue), no progress output even if `CI` is set, a one-line result (also `0 issues`), and `[*]` after each issue `--alter` can fix. An explicit `--output-format` wins, and nothing changes outside an agent. See [AI agents](https://psalm.dev/docs/running_psalm/ai_agents/). (#15068, #15069, #15067, @alies-dev)
- **Crash reports** name the plugin and hook that threw and the statement Psalm was analysing, save the full report to a file, and print a link that opens a prefilled issue on Psalm's or the plugin's tracker. (#15070, @alies-dev)
- **`--no-taint-analysis`** skips taint analysis for one run (`runTaintAnalysis` is on by default), e.g. for a quick local check (#15078, @orklah). 
- **New issues**:
  - `InternalFunction` for a call of an `@internal` or `@psalm-internal` function from outside its namespace. (#15084, @orklah)
  - `ParseError` for constructor property promotion when analysing PHP 7.x. (#15086, @orklah)
- **`--alter` on PHP 8.2** writes `true`, `false` and `null` as native types (`: true|null` instead of `: bool|null` plus a docblock), and no longer adds docblocks that repeat a native type. (#15083, @orklah)

## Performance

- Narrowing a variable no longer copies the whole scope for every other variable, which made 7.18 about 2% slower than 7.17. (#15121, @alies-dev)

## Fixes

### Taint analysis

- `TaintedCallable` for a tainted method name: `$object->$name()`, `A::$name()`. (#15072, @alies-dev)
- `strip_tags()` with allowed tags is not an html escape: `strip_tags($_GET["x"], "<a>")` is `TaintedHtml`. (#14753, @arpitjain099)

### Stubs and plugins

- A stub's `@return` (or its own `@psalm-overload`) replaces the original's `@return $this` and overloads, so a stubbed call returns the stub's type again (a 7.19.0 regression). (#15090, @alies-dev)
- No false `MethodSignatureMismatch` for an override that widens a param of a stubbed userland class, and `float`/`int` swaps PHP rejects are reported. (#15114, @orklah)
- `[]` on `Ds\Map`, `Ds\Vector` and other Ds collections is typed and checked, and a stub class that leaves out a method of its interfaces still has it. (#15039, @orklah)
- A function params provider returning `null` keeps the function's params checked. (#15040, @orklah)
- Params providers can resolve `[$this, 'method']`: `CallAnalyzer::getFunctionIdsFromCallableArg()` takes the call's `Context`. (#15082, @orklah)
- A return type provider of a class wins over its `@mixin` for a method behind `__call()`/`__callStatic()`. (#15020, @shu-chen-dot-ca)

### Arrays and narrowing

- `isset()` and `!isset()` on array offsets: a negated check drops the shapes that always have the offset and keeps the optional offsets it leaves; an empty array stays empty; a nested `isset($a["x"][3])` narrows `$a["x"]`. (#15103, #15104, #15105, #15076

Psalm

[![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm coverage](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/coverage.svg?)](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm level](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/level.svg?)](https://psalm.dev/) Psalm is a static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. [Join the official Psalm news channel](https://t.me/psalmphp) and the Psalm community on [Telegram](https://t.me/psalmphp_community) and [Discord](https://discord.gg/RwH8rEpxt9)! ## Installation To get started, check out the [installation guide](docs/running_psalm/installation.md). ## Live Demo You can play around with Psalm [on its website](https://psalm.dev/). ## Documentation Documentation is available on [Psalm’s website](https://psalm.dev/docs), generated from the [docs](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/master/docs) folder. ## Support Psalm development You can support Psalm development by requesting a support contract from [Daniil Gentili](https://daniil.it), the only active maintainer of Psalm. Support contracts can cover full integration of Psalm into existing codebases, support for Psalm issues and development of additional Psalm features. See [here »](https://daniil.it) for info, pricing and contact information. ## Interested in contributing? Have a look at [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Who made this Built by Matt Brown ([@muglug](https://github.com/muglug)). Maintained by Daniil Gentili ([@danog](https://github.com/danog)), Alies Lapatsin ([@alies-dev](https://github.com/alies-dev)) and Orklah ([@orklah](https://github.com/orklah)). Former maintainer: Bruce Weirdan ([@weirdan](https://github.com/weirdan)). The engineering team at [Vimeo](https://github.com/vimeo) have provided a lot encouragement, especially [@nbeliard](https://github.com/nbeliard), [@erunion](https://github.com/erunion) and [@nickyr](https://github.com/nickyr).
